the development of a near‐infrared‐transparent black dye based on a diketopyyrrolopyrrol (DPP) derivative and its application as an optical filter for night vision photography, security imaging and forensic applications is described.

a supramolecular black gel is formed by a diketopyrolopyrroles based low molecular weight organogelator and the nanocomposite of the black gel with polydimethylsiloxane exhibits high NIR transparency.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new NIR‐transmit‐ing black material for security and forensic imaging applications, which can be fabricated into a thin film for practical use.
the synthesis and characterization of a novel supranolecular NIR‐transparent material for security and forensic‐related imaging applications.
the design of NIR‐transparent black nanocomposites based on supramolecular chemistry for practical applications.

this work demonstrates a new approach to the synthesis of black materials that are NIR transparent, and the potential of such materials in security imaging and forensic applications.
the developed supramolecular nanocomposite is a promising candidate for the fabrication of NIR‐transmit‐only filters for security and forensic applications.
a novel supramolecules-based black dye from diketopyrrolepyrrole (DP) was developed.

we have developed a new NIR‐transmit‐only black material that can be used for a variety of applications including security imaging, night vision, and forensic applications.
the developed nanocomposite is a novel and practical material that is capable of NIR‐transparent imaging for security and forensic applications.
we developed a new supramolecular NIR‐transmit‐ing elastomer from a low molecular weight organogelator for security and forensic applications.

the supramolecular approach provides a facile route for the fabrication of a NIR‐transparent elastomer with tunable optical properties.
